notes: KNOWN FAILING — Hermes 0.19.0 genuinely backgrounds: `terminal(background=true)` calls process_registry.spawn_local, which Popens the command through the login shell with start_new_session=True (a detached child that outlives the tool call) and returns immediately with {"output":"Background process started","session_id":"proc_<hex12>","pid":<int>}; the companion `process` tool polls it and reports "status":"exited". Both tools are in _HERMES_CORE_TOOLS, so this is default CLI traffic. BUT the hermes adapter has NO background-process tracking, in two places: parser.go's ParseLine never sets ev.BackgroundSpawns, and — because Source is agent.ProcessOwnedStore — metrics.go's foldMessages bypasses the TranscriptTailer entirely, folding only open tools/tasks/waiting-cue, so SessionMetrics.BackgroundProcessCount and BackgroundProcessPIDs are never set. watcher.go's turnIsDone then marks the turn done as soon as the newest row is an assistant row with finish_reason='stop'. RECIPE: the prompt spawns `sleep 40 && echo BG_DONE` with background=true and replies `started` IMMEDIATELY — no polling, no notify_on_complete — so the turn's 'stop' row lands ~10s in while the 40s process is still alive. A poll-to-completion recipe (the claudecode shape) would be VACUOUS on hermes: hermes emits no intra-turn turn-end marker, so the working span would be held by the open turn rather than by background tracking. CORRECT arc: ready→working at the prompt, working HELD past the 'stop' row until the detached process exits (~48s after turn start), then a single working→ready. bg_alive_working asserts working persists 25000ms — longer than the ~10s turn, well inside the 40s bg lifetime — so the daemon settling to ready at turn end makes this phase EXPECTED to fail. Fix is the hermes parallel of #450/#661: emit BackgroundSpawn{BashID: pid} from the terminal-background tool result, drop it on a `process` poll reporting "status":"exited", and carry the open set through messageFold into BackgroundProcessCount + BackgroundProcessPIDs (the PID probe, not lsof — spawn_local buffers stdout through a pipe and writes no output file on the local backend). Re-record and clear known_failing then. Hermes' session row is INSERTed on the first user message, not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first, so session_birth is anchored to start UNPINNED and every later phase chains via same_session_as. `model` is deliberately NOT pinned: the recording home's config.yaml is provisioned at record time, so record fills it from the recording.

text: The hermes session appears in ready. Unpinned: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after it), not at launch, and a transient proc-<PID> presession may appear first.
The prompt drives the hermes session ready → working; the terminal(background=true) call auto-executes (sleep 40 && echo BG_DONE is not a dangerous command, so no approval window opens).

While the detached terminal(background=true) process (sleep 40) is alive, the session must stay working — it must NOT settle to ready when the turn's own finish_reason='stop' row lands (~10s in). KNOWN FAILING: the hermes adapter tracks no background processes, so it settles to ready at that stop row — well before the 25000 ms hold this phase requires.

After the last background process exits (~48s after turn start; with no store row to key on, the daemon's PID liveness probe is the only signal), the session settles working → ready on the SAME session — exactly one such transition.
